text:
"Bussi steals two points for Carolina," Cory Lavalette posted when it was over, and it is hard to argue. Brandon Bussi, the undrafted goalie who earned his way up from the AHL, stopped 32 of 33 in a 3-1 win in Tampa, saving about 1.8 goals more than those shots deserved. The Lightning out-attempted Carolina 69 to 55 and, by shot quality, would win this game about 57% of the time. They won it zero times on the night that counted.

Tampa got the only goal of the first 45 minutes. Anthony Cirelli scored on the power play 55 seconds into the second period, from Jake Guentzel and Nikita Kucherov, and the Lightning owned that period, out-chancing Carolina 1.59 to 1.01 in expected goals (the quality of chances created). Andrei Vasilevskiy was good at the other end too, stopping a 22% chance from Mark Jankowski. With Kucherov's name all over the trade and contract rumours this month (Elliotte Friedman has floated a Montreal plan), a 1-0 lead built on his assist would have been a tidy story for Tampa.

Then Eric Robinson happened, again. He scored on a 4% chance at 5:24 of the third, unassisted, and Lavalette noted it was his sixth goal in 18 career regular-season games against Vasilevskiy. Ninety-seven seconds later, a Seth Jarvis block led to a rush and Jaccob Slavin scored his first goal of the season, the biggest swing of the night, taking Carolina from 48% to 77% to win. Bussi's best moment came late, a stop on Jake Guentzel that our numbers count as the game's biggest save, and Jackson Blake finished it with 35 seconds left.

The Hurricanes have now won three straight, this one without the injured Nikolaj Ehlers. It was not their best game. It was the kind they will need when the shots are not going their way.
headline: Brandon Bussi steals one in Tampa
